name: sweet-spot
summary: Hands a long session over before the context gets too big: to a fresh session that starts from a handoff, or by Claude Code's own /compact.
description: sweet-spot keeps the context of a Claude Code session in the range where it is big enough to hold the work and still small enough to be cheap and reliable. Past a threshold (200k tokens by default) it waits for a pause at the end of an answer, counts down above the prompt with a "Not now", and then hands the session over.

By default Claude writes a handoff, the mod clears the session and submits the text of the handoff as the first message of a fresh one. If that fails, it compacts the session with Claude Code's own /compact instead. The old session stays as it was, and /resume takes you back to it.

It never acts in the middle of a turn, and a turn that ended in an error, a refusal or Esc is no pause. While a subagent, a background task or a timer is running it postpones, up to an emergency brake 150k tokens past the threshold. A dev server or a watcher does not hold it back; the fresh session is told it still runs. What you type during a handover is held and goes in when it is done.

With an hour of prompt cache it also writes a handoff shortly before the cache expires in a long pause, so a message sent after it has expired starts a fresh session instead of sending the whole conversation again.
It writes no files, makes no network calls and starts one process only: tail, to read the end of a transcript above 4 MiB. It is a community project, not made or endorsed by Anthropic.
notice: Developed against Claude Code 2.1.296; older versions are not tested, and versions before 2.1.271 cannot load the mod at all. It installs from its own repository's marketplace, not from Anthropic's.

guide.title: What it does
paragraphs: At the end of an answer it looks at the context size. Past the threshold, and when nothing else is going on, a line above the prompt counts down countdown_seconds (10 by default). Key 1 in an empty prompt moves the handover back; typing or sending a message stops the countdown without moving anything, and the next pause counts down again.

/sweet-spot status shows the context against the window, where the next handover comes and the emergency brake. /sweet-spot later 50k moves one handover back by 50k tokens, /sweet-spot asap hands over at the next pause wherever the context stands, and /sweet-spot redeliver submits a held message again if delivering it failed.

guide.title: Handoff or compact
paragraphs: handoff_method picks the way and handoff_fallback the one tried when it fails before it changed the session. internal-handoff (the default) writes a handoff with a built-in prompt, which ~/.claude/sweet-spot/handoff-prompt.md replaces. builtin-compact is Claude Code's own /compact, and the session stays. external-command runs a handoff command of your own and reads its file.
Measured in real handovers, a fresh session starts at 62k to 98k tokens. A threshold below 130000 is refused with the reason, and the mod stays off.

guide.title: How it works
paragraphs: ui.render draws the countdown above the prompt and command.run answers /sweet-spot. The other events tell it when a turn starts, steps and completes, what is typed and submitted, which tools run, and when a session starts, ends or is compacted: turn.start, turn.step, turn.complete, prompt.edit, prompt.submit, tool.call, session.start, session.end and session.compact. It also registers the classic events Stop, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, PermissionRequest and PostModelSwitch.

It reads the session transcript to learn how long its prompt cache lives, the handoff file, the optional handoff prompt, a listing of the temp directory to find a handoff, and the environment variables HOME and TMPDIR. To check this against the code, run claude plugin validate . in the repository: it lists every call the hooks make and every environment variable they read.

guide.title: Set up
paragraphs: Inside Claude Code, add the marketplace and install the mod, then run /reload-plugins. The settings are in the /config menu under sweet-spot. To watch first, turn dry_run on: then it only says when it would hand over.

guide.title: Download the source
paragraphs: Clone the repository and load it as a plugin folder. To run its tests, run claude plugin test . in that folder.
